title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
header: Date: 2026-12-02 | Time: 11:00 AM PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Matt Collins (Redwood AE), Sergio Vega (Redwood SE), Anna Li (DataWave PM), Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra), Priya Rao (DataWave ML)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood against baseline provider. Discussed p95 latency, throughput (RPS and tokens/sec), cold vs warm cache effects, batching and quantization tradeoffs, and next steps for a production-like canary. Customer emphasized VPC/KMS requirements, SOC2 questions, and a desire to validate H100-backed Dedicated pool. Action items: share detailed benchmark sheet, schedule on-prem / VPC security review, enable dedicated trial for 2 weeks.
topics: batching window and batch size tuning
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Matt Collins - Share annotated benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs by EOD 2026-12-02
Sergio Vega - Provide Redwood config used for the run (batching/window/kv cache settings) by 2026-12-03
Priya Rao - Run 3rd-party baseline rerun with fixed seq=512 and upload results by 2026-12-06
Jamal Ahmed - Provision VPC peering details and KMS policy for test env by 2026-12-07
Anna Li - Confirm exec success criteria and pilot sign-off date by 2026-12-08
next_steps: Redwood to share full benchmark sheet and config (Matt)
Customer to rerun baseline with seq=512 and warm cache sample (Priya)
Schedule security deep-dive with infra and security teams (Jamal + Redwood)
Provision Dedicated trial (H100-backed) for 2 weeks and run production traffic sampling
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1: okay hey everyone welcome, um this is the weekly poc sync from redwood side we've got matt and sergio here, shout out if i missed anyone
00:06 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): hey all, matt here, quick agenda \u0002 benchmark recap, key diffs vs baseline, tuning suggestions, action items
00:12 Anna Li (DataWave PM): thanks matt, appreciate it. we mostly want to see p95 numbers and what to expect at 90k tokens/day pattern \u0002 and talk security stuff later
00:20 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): cool i pulled the latest runs \u0002 two main tests: "warm-cache" steady state and "cold-cache" cold start. baseline provider was ProviderX's managed endpoint. redwood run used Dedicated (trial farm) on H100s, model quantized int8, batch window 20ms, max batch size 64
00:38 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): quick q \u0002 when you say int8 was that post-training quant or runtime kernel path?
00:42 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): runtime quantization via our optimized kernel, not PTQ; it's a quant-friendly execution path, some slight accuracy delta we measured ~0.5% on rouge/qa sets
00:50 Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra): can you just state the headline p95 numbers again? we had trouble reading the sheet
00:55 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): sure. warm-cache p95 latency for 512-seq was 140ms on redwood (H100 dedicated), baseline ProviderX was 210ms. throughput steady-state tokens/sec was 18k tokens/sec for redwood vs 12k for baseline. cold-cache p95 spikes were higher \u0002 redwood 420ms vs baseline 600ms for first requests
01:15 Anna Li (DataWave PM): okay that's promising, so roughly 30-35% improvement latency and 50% throughput uplift, right?
01:22 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): roughly, though depends on sequence length; at seq=1024 the gap narrows a bit \u0002 redwood 260ms p95 vs baseline 330ms p95 on those runs
01:31 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): what about tokenization and batching effects? are you batching across requests at the api layer or server runtime?
01:36 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): both. we do continuous batching in the runtime. for these runs we configured api-level batching window 20ms and kernel-level batching capacity was sufficient. also enabled prefix kv caching for repeated prompts \u0002 that reduced per-token compute in rerun scenarios by ~18%
01:53 Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra): curious about GPU util and tail latencies \u0002 any quant numbers?
01:57 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): GPU util avg was 68% during steady runs; tail p99 is about 2.4s for cold-cache tests, but p95 remains in the 140-260ms range depending on seq. baseline p99 was worse, around 3.6s
02:13 Anna Li (DataWave PM): ok. you mentioned quantization accuracy earlier \u0002 priya is worried about hallucination delta for our knowledge-base applic. can you quantify the 0.5%?
02:22 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): that 0.5% was on our internal QA holdout \u0002 short answer, negligible for most generation tasks; we can run your eval set and produce exact deltas. tradeoff is cost/latency vs small accuracy change
02:34 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): please run against our evals. we'll share the prompt set after this call
02:39 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): noted. on security questions \u0002 we support SOC2, SSO via SAML/Okta, KMS integration and audit logs. jamal, you flagged KMS policy details last week?
02:49 Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra): yeah we need to see key wrapping and rotation docs and also whether logs can be shipped to our SIEM. also we want to validate VPC peering and private endpoint options
02:58 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): absolutely \u0002 we have a private deployment option with customer-managed VPC and can provide HSM/KMS integration. audit logs can be delivered to your cloud storage or SIEM endpoint. we'll schedule a security deep dive to go through specifics
03:12 Anna Li (DataWave PM): thanks. back to perf \u0002 any anomalies between runs? i noticed one run at 11:14 had a sudden latency spike even in warm-cache
03:19 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): saw that \u0002 that was an autoscaling event on the baseline infra during their test window, i think they were throttling other tenants. our dedicated H100 pool had microseconds jitter from GC on the control plane but didn't affect p95 significantly
03:33 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): can you clarify the baseline config? i.e. were they using sequence 512 or 1024, what batch window?
03:38 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): baseline used default provider settings: seq=512 for most tests but a couple seq=1024 runs were in the sheet. they had batching window 50ms and no prefix kv cache enabled. that's part of why we see the gap
03:50 Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra): from our side we want to reproduce baseline exactly before we change too much. i'll have priya re-run and upload the logs
03:55 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): yup we'll do that \u0002 also we'll run an int4 variant to see model behavior, though int4 on our evals may show higher accuracy drift
04:03 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): note int4 is available but we generally recommend int8 for this workload; int4 can be faster but accuracy regressions are more likely. we can run both and show diffs
04:12 Anna Li (DataWave PM): what's needed to spin up a two-week dedicated H100 trial? cost and timeline?
04:18 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): we can provision a dedicated trial in 48-72 hours once you sign the trial SoW. cost is covered under the pilot budget we discussed, but we'll send a formal quote. the trial gives you isolated H100 capacity and a private endpoint into your VPC if desired
04:31 Jamal Ahmed (DataWave Infra): ok please include network diagram and egress rules in the doc. also need to confirm backup rotation with KMS
04:38 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): will do. i'll include a network diagram and sample KMS policy in the packet
04:43 Priya Rao (DataWave ML): one more technical \u0002 how do you handle prefetched KV cache eviction on model rollouts? we worry about stale cache during canary
04:50 Sergio Vega (Redwood SE): good question \u0002 we version cache by model id and rollout tag; during rollout we maintain dual caches and route old tokens to the compat path. eviction is time+LRU based; we can coordinate cache flushes during the canary step to avoid surprises
05:05 Anna Li (DataWave PM): great, let's recap next steps and owners please
05:10 Matt Collins (Redwood AE): recap: matt to share benchmark sheet and config, sergio share runtime flags, priya run baseline rerun, jamal provide VPC/KMS details, anna confirm success criteria and sign-off timeline. schedule security deep-dive next week. dedicated trial provisioning pending SoW
05:28 Anna Li (DataWave PM): thanks all, that works for us
05:31 Speaker 1: wrap up \u0002 end of meeting
